nodes.label: Absolute prohibition on fabricated facts
nodes.rationale: A hard fail, not a score reduction. The Princeton GEO work (KDD 2024) showed a lift from fabrication against GPT-3.5 in 2023, but it is now trained on as an adversarial signal, creates FTC §5 exposure, and the lift evaporates under competition (C-SEO Bench, NeurIPS 2025); real evidence in the same structural pattern captures 80-90% of the effect with none of the risk.

nodes.label: Humanization guards
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from the humanizer methodology, the only surveyed skill treating de-AI-ing as measurable engineering: S1/S2/S3 severity, an A-D grade on the result rather than the input, a 50% change-rate guard, a mandatory semantic-preservation self-check, and a density threshold above which patching is futile.

nodes.label: Task analysis method

nodes.label: Flow design rules

nodes.label: Vision alignment — hard rule (super-ux)

nodes.label: Misaligned protocol — name, offer two paths, wait
nodes.rationale: Stop before writing code: name the conflict quoting the layer it contradicts, offer either reshaping the feature to fit or amending the vision with the cost stated, then wait for the decision. Do not pick one silently — the agent proposes, the human decides which layer moves.

nodes.label: Do NOT trigger for bug fixes, refactors, tests, docs

nodes.label: vision.md template (nine sections)
nodes.rationale: Owned by the vision skill; the headings and their order are what docs/ux/lint.py keys off. Writing the file is half the job — the other half is the hard-rule block in the project's instruction file, without which nothing ever reads the document.
nodes.norm_label: vision.md template (nine sections)

nodes.label: 1. Essence
nodes.rationale: One sentence with no feature names, UI or technology. Test: would it survive a total rewrite on a different stack? If not, it names an implementation.
nodes.norm_label: 1. essence

nodes.label: 2. Core idea
nodes.rationale: An observation about the world, not a problem statement — X is abundant, Y is scarce, this product bridges the gap. One observation, not a list.
nodes.norm_label: 2. core idea

nodes.label: 3. What the system does
nodes.rationale: Continuous behaviour in verbs, not nouns — 'has a dashboard' is not behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: 3. what the system does

nodes.label: 4. The user's role
nodes.rationale: What the user becomes — directs, judges, decides. If it reads like operating any other tool, go deeper.
nodes.norm_label: 4. the user's role

nodes.label: 5. Principles
nodes.rationale: Three to five, each 'we do X, not Y' where Y is something a reasonable team would genuinely have picked. A principle with no rejected side is a slogan.
nodes.norm_label: 5. principles

nodes.label: 6. Anti-vision
nodes.rationale: What the product refuses to become, naming the adjacent products it could drift into and saying no to each. This is the layer teams skip and the only one that ever settles an argument.
nodes.norm_label: 6. anti-vision

nodes.label: 7. Horizon
nodes.rationale: Two to three years as a direction, not a roadmap — roadmaps belong in the tracker and go stale in a quarter.
nodes.norm_label: 7. horizon

nodes.label: 8. The one sentence
nodes.norm_label: 8. the one sentence

nodes.label: 9. The alignment test
nodes.rationale: Three to five questions any proposed feature must pass — what the hard rule in the instruction file actually runs. A stranger should be able to reject a plausible feature with them.
nodes.norm_label: 9. the alignment test
